# What is a tissue?

<!-- STEP id="amoeba" -->
## One cell does it all

In an amoeba, the one cell does every job of life. Nothing can be shared out, because there is only one cell.

<!-- STEP id="groups" -->
## Groups of similar cells

In a many-celled body, cells that are alike in structure sit together and do the same work. **A tissue is a group of cells, similar in structure, that work together to perform a specific function.**

<!-- STEP id="animal" -->
## Tissues in animals

In animals, muscle tissue makes movement, such as bending your arm to lift a school bag. Nervous tissue carries messages to different parts of the body, so your hand pulls away from a hot tawa.

<!-- STEP id="plant" -->
## Tissues in plants

Plants have tissues too. Their conducting tissues share the work of transport: xylem carries water and minerals, while phloem carries food. In each case, one group of similar cells does one kind of job for the whole living thing.
